title: Request, approve, expire, remove: one cycle
lede: A person or an agent asks for time-bound access. Privilege routes the request, an approver acts in chat, the platform gets a grant that carries an expiry, a receipt is written, and a reaper removes the access when the window closes. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Simulated.

nodes.label: Platform: GitHub, GitLab, Salesforce, Snowflake, Databricks, Google

steps.title: Request
steps.what: The requester picks a platform, a resource, a level, a duration and a reason. A request with no expiry cannot be made. Agents and people use the same request.

steps.title: Ask the approver
steps.what: Privilege routes the request to the right approver for the first level of the policy's chain: the manager, the owner of the resource, the security group or the data owner. Never the requester.

steps.title: Approve or deny
steps.what: The approver acts directly from Slack or Mattermost, or in the console. Self-approval is refused, an agent cannot approve, and an expired request cannot be approved.

steps.title: Notify and ticket
steps.what: Microsoft Teams, Jira and ServiceNow only receive notifications and tickets: they cannot approve.

steps.title: Grant with expiry
steps.what: When the last level approves, the platform gets the access. The grant carries the expiry from the start.

steps.title: Write the receipt
steps.what: Every grant is recorded in a receipt chained to the one before it, with its reference count when policies overlap.

steps.title: Expiry list
steps.what: The reaper works from the receipts, not from the request that created them, so it still acts when the original workflow is long finished.

steps.title: Remove at expiry
steps.what: When the last reference expires the access is removed from the platform. If another grant still holds it, the platform keeps it.
